concepts_used: Dyarchy: Mechanism and Division of Subjects at Provincial Level

shared.concept_anchor: Dyarchy: reserved vs transferred subjects classification

en.display_text:
Under the dyarchy system introduced by the Government of India Act 1919, which of the following subjects was administered by ministers responsible to the provincial legislature?

(a) Law and order
(b) Public health
(c) Agriculture — because it was linked to land revenue
(d) Finance
en.strong_distractor: c — Option c is deceptive because agriculture feels like a revenue-generating, government-controlled function, leading students to classify it as reserved alongside land revenue.
elimination_logic: Identify the core principle: reserved subjects were those the Governor administered with his Executive Council, retained under British control due to revenue or security concerns.
Eliminate option (a): law and order was a reserved subject — it belonged to the Governor's executive council, not to elected ministers.
Eliminate option (c): agriculture was a transferred subject administered by ministers responsible to the legislature — not reserved.
Eliminate option (d): finance was a reserved subject — the deliberate withholding of financial control was the central flaw critics identified in dyarchy.
Confirm option (b): public health was a transferred subject, making it the correct answer as the one correctly identified transferred subject.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap here exploits the intuitive expectation that agriculture — involving land, revenue, and economic control — would be a reserved subject. Students who reason by analogy with 'land revenue' (which was indeed reserved) frequently misclassify agriculture. However, agriculture was transferred precisely because the British wanted elected ministers to take responsibility for slow-developing rural welfare functions, while keeping revenue collection under bureaucratic control.
en.final_explanation:
Dyarchy under the Government of India Act 1919 divided provincial subjects into two categories. Reserved subjects — including law and order, finance, land revenue, and irrigation — were administered by the Governor with his Executive Council of appointed officials. Transferred subjects — including education, public health, agriculture, and local self-government — were placed under ministers who were responsible to the elected legislature.

• Option (a): Law and order — Incorrect identification as transferred. It was firmly reserved — a security function never delegated to elected ministers.
• Option (b): Public health — Correct. Public health was a transferred subject administered by elected ministers, making this the correct answer.
• Option (c): Agriculture — Incorrect identification as reserved. Agriculture was a transferred subject, though critics noted it was hamstrung because finance remained reserved.
• Option (d): Finance — Incorrect identification as transferred. Finance was the most jealously reserved subject — its retention by the Governor made transferred subjects essentially unworkable.

Value Addition:
• The irony of dyarchy: transferred ministers were accountable to legislatures for subjects they lacked funds to administer.
• Under the Government of India Act 1935, dyarchy was abolished at the provincial level and provinces received full autonomy — dyarchy was instead proposed (but never implemented) at the Centre.
• 'Dyarchy' literally means 'double government' — coined to describe the dual executive at the provincial level.

hi.display_text:
1919 के गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट द्वारा लागू ड्युअर्की प्रणाली के तहत, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विषय प्रांतीय विधानसभा के प्रति जिम्मेदार मंत्रियों द्वारा प्रशासित किया जाता था?

(a) कानून और व्यवस्था
(b) सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य
(c) कृषि — क्योंकि यह भूमि राजस्व से जुड़ा था
(d) वित्त
hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प c भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि कृषि राजस्व-सृजन, सरकार नियंत्रित कार्य प्रतीत होता है, जिससे छात्र इसे भूमि राजस्व के साथ आरक्षित वर्ग में वर्गीकृत करते हैं।
elimination_logic: मूल सिद्धांत की पहचान करें: आरक्षित विषय वे थे जिन्हें गवर्नर अपने कार्यकारी परिषद के साथ प्रशासित करता था, जो राजस्व या सुरक्षा कारणों से ब्रिटिश नियंत्रण में रखे गए थे।
(a) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: कानून और व्यवस्था एक आरक्षित विषय था — यह गवर्नर की कार्यकारी परिषद का था, निर्वाचित मंत्रियों का नहीं।
(c) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: कृषि एक हस्तांतरित विषय था जिसे विधायिका के प्रति जिम्मेदार मंत्रियों द्वारा प्रशासित किया जाता था — यह आरक्षित नहीं था।
(d) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: वित्त एक आरक्षित विषय था — वित्तीय नियंत्रण को जानबूझकर रोका जाना ड्युअर्की की मुख्य कमी थी जिसे आलोचकों ने पहचाना।
(b) विकल्प की पुष्टि करें: सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य एक हस्तांतरित विषय था, जो इसे सही उत्तर बनाता है क्योंकि इसे सही ढंग से हस्तांतरित विषय के रूप में पहचाना गया।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह जाल इस सहज अपेक्षा का फायदा उठाता है कि कृषि — जो भूमि, राजस्व और आर्थिक नियंत्रण से जुड़ी है — एक आरक्षित विषय होगा। छात्र जो 'भूमि राजस्व' (जो वास्तव में आरक्षित था) के साथ तुलना करते हैं, वे अक्सर कृषि को गलत वर्गीकृत कर देते हैं। हालांकि, कृषि हस्तांतरित थी क्योंकि ब्रिटिश चाहते थे कि निर्वाचित मंत्री ग्रामीण कल्याण के धीमे विकास वाले कार्यों की जिम्मेदारी लें, जबकि राजस्व संग्रह को नौकरशाही नियंत्रण में रखा गया।
hi.final_explanation:
1919 के गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट के तहत ड्युअर्की ने प्रांतीय विषयों को दो श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया। आरक्षित विषय — जिनमें कानून और व्यवस्था, वित्त, भूमि राजस्व, और सिंचाई शामिल थे — गवर्नर द्वारा उनके कार्यकारी परिषद के साथ प्रशासित किए जाते थे। हस्तांतरित विषय — जिनमें शिक्षा, सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य, कृषि, और स्थानीय स्वशासन शामिल थे — मंत्रियों के अधीन थे जो निर्वाचित विधानसभा के प्रति जिम्मेदार थे।

• विकल्प (a): कानून और व्यवस्था — हस्तांतरित के रूप में गलत पहचान। यह दृढ़ता से आरक्षित था — एक सुरक्षा कार्य जिसे कभी निर्वाचित मंत्रियों को सौंपा नहीं गया।
• विकल्प (b): सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य — सही। सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य एक हस्तांतरित विषय था जिसे निर्वाचित मंत्रियों द्वारा प्रशासित किया जाता था, इसलिए यह सही उत्तर है।
• विकल्प (c): कृषि — आरक्षित के रूप में गलत पहचान। कृषि एक हस्तांतरित विषय था, हालांकि आलोचकों ने नोट किया कि यह वित्त के आरक्षित रहने के कारण बाधित था।
• विकल्प (d): वित्त — हस्तांतरित के रूप में गलत पहचान। वित्त सबसे अधिक सावधानी से आरक्षित विषय था — गवर्नर द्वारा इसका नियंत्रण बनाए रखना हस्तांतरित विषयों को व्यावहारिक रूप से असंभव बनाता था।

Value Addition:
• ड्युअर्की की विडंबना: हस्तांतरित मंत्री उन विषयों के लिए विधानसभा के प्रति जवाबदेह थे जिनके लिए उनके पास प्रशासन के लिए धन नहीं था।
• 1935 के गवर्नमेंट ऑफ इंडिया एक्ट के तहत, प्रांतीय स्तर पर ड्युअर्की समाप्त कर दी गई और प्रांतों को पूर्ण स्वायत्तता मिली — ड्युअर्की केंद्र में प्रस्तावित थी (लेकिन कभी लागू नहीं हुई)।
• 'ड्युअर्की' का शाब्दिक अर्थ है 'दोहरी सरकार' — जो प्रांतीय स्तर पर द्वि-कार्यकारी को दर्शाने के लिए गढ़ा गया।

shared.concept_anchor: Montagu Declaration 1917 vs Montagu-Chelmsford Report 1918

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Montagu Declaration of 1917 and the Montagu-Chelmsford Report:

1. The Montagu Declaration of 1917 promised the 'immediate grant of self-government' to India as an explicit policy objective.
2. Edwin Montagu, who issued the 1917 Declaration, held the office of Secretary of State for India at the time.
3. The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, which preceded the Government of India Act 1919, was published in 1918.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Montagu Declaration of 1917 promised the 'immediate grant of self-government' to India as an explicit policy objective.
statement_analysis.reason: The Declaration used the phrase 'gradual development of self-governing institutions' — the word 'gradual' was deliberate and significant, explicitly ruling out any immediate transfer of power.

statement_analysis.statement: Edwin Montagu, who issued the 1917 Declaration, held the office of Secretary of State for India at the time.
statement_analysis.reason: Edwin Montagu was the Secretary of State for India, while Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy — the two offices are frequently confused in UPSC questions.

statement_analysis.statement: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, which preceded the Government of India Act 1919, was published in 1918.
statement_analysis.reason: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was published in 1918, distinct from the Montagu Declaration of 1917 — these are two separate documents produced a year apart.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is tempting because statements 2 and 3 are factually precise, and students who are uncertain about statement 1 may assume the Declaration used stronger language than it did.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: The Declaration's language was 'gradual development of self-governing institutions' — not 'immediate grant of self-government.' Statement 1 is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 2: Montagu was Secretary of State for India; Chelmsford was Viceroy. Statement 2 is correct.
Evaluate Statement 3: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was published in 1918, one year after the 1917 Declaration. Statement 3 is correct.
Only Statements 2 and 3 are correct — select option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the word 'gradual' — a term the British used deliberately to deflect the demand for immediate self-rule. Students who recall the Declaration's promise of 'responsible government' but not its exact qualifying language may mark Statement 1 as correct. UPSC has historically tested this precise qualifier because it is the difference between a genuine constitutional commitment and a carefully hedged colonial concession.
en.final_explanation:
The Montagu Declaration of August 1917 was the first explicit acknowledgment by the British government that responsible government for India was a policy goal. However, it was heavily qualified — the phrase used was 'gradual development of self-governing institutions,' not any promise of immediate or dominion-level self-government.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: The word 'immediate' does not appear anywhere in the Declaration. 'Gradual' was the operative qualifier, and nationalists criticized it precisely for this hedging.
• Statement 2 — Correct: Edwin Montagu served as Secretary of State for India. Lord Chelmsford was the concurrent Viceroy of India — their roles are commonly swapped in traps.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, the joint document recommending constitutional reforms, was published in 1918. The Act itself came in 1919 — three separate milestones in three consecutive years.

Value Addition:
• The 1917 Declaration is considered constitutionally significant as the first time 'responsible government' appeared as an explicitly stated British aim for India.
• It did NOT promise Dominion Status — nationalists, especially Annie Besant and Tilak, found it far too timid.
• The Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) formed the basis for the Government of India Act 1919, which received Royal Assent in December 1919.

hi.display_text:
1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा और मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

1. 1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा ने भारत को 'तत्काल स्वशासन' देने का स्पष्ट नीति उद्देश्य वादा किया था।
2. एडविन मोंटागु, जिन्होंने 1917 की घोषणा जारी की, उस समय भारत के सचिव थे।
3. मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट, जो भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 से पहले आई, 1918 में प्रकाशित हुई थी।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1 और 2
(b) केवल 1 और 3
(c) केवल 2 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Montagu Declaration of 1917 promised the 'immediate grant of self-government' to India as an explicit policy objective.
statement_analysis.reason: घोषणा में 'स्वशासी संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास' शब्दावली का उपयोग किया गया था — 'क्रमिक' शब्द जानबूझकर और महत्वपूर्ण था, जो स्पष्ट रूप से किसी भी तत्काल सत्ता हस्तांतरण को अस्वीकार करता था।

statement_analysis.statement: Edwin Montagu, who issued the 1917 Declaration, held the office of Secretary of State for India at the time.
statement_analysis.reason: एडविन मोंटागु उस समय भारत के सचिव (Secretary of State for India) थे, जबकि लॉर्ड चेल्म्सफोर्ड वायसराय थे — ये दोनों पद UPSC प्रश्नों में अक्सर भ्रमित किए जाते हैं।

statement_analysis.statement: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, which preceded the Government of India Act 1919, was published in 1918.
statement_analysis.reason: मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट 1918 में प्रकाशित हुई थी, जो 1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा से अलग है — ये दो अलग दस्तावेज हैं जो एक वर्ष के अंतराल पर बने।

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (तीनों सही) आकर्षक है क्योंकि कथन 2 और 3 तथ्यात्मक रूप से सटीक हैं, और जो छात्र कथन 1 के बारे में अनिश्चित हैं वे मान सकते हैं कि घोषणा ने उससे अधिक मजबूत भाषा का उपयोग किया था।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 का मूल्यांकन करें: घोषणा की भाषा 'स्वशासी संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास' थी — 'तत्काल स्वशासन का अनुदान' नहीं। अतः कथन 1 गलत है।
कथन 2 का मूल्यांकन करें: मोंटागु भारत के सचिव थे; चेल्म्सफोर्ड वायसराय थे। अतः कथन 2 सही है।
कथन 3 का मूल्यांकन करें: मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट 1918 में प्रकाशित हुई, जो 1917 की घोषणा के एक वर्ष बाद थी। अतः कथन 3 सही है।
केवल कथन 2 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (c) चुनें।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: फंदा 'क्रमिक' शब्द में है — यह ब्रिटिशों द्वारा तत्काल स्वशासन की मांग को टालने के लिए जानबूझकर इस्तेमाल किया गया था। जो छात्र घोषणा में 'जिम्मेदार सरकार' का वादा याद रखते हैं लेकिन इसकी सटीक शर्तों को नहीं, वे कथन 1 को सही मान सकते हैं। UPSC ने इस सटीक शर्त को परखा है क्योंकि यह एक वास्तविक संवैधानिक प्रतिबद्धता और सावधानीपूर्वक सीमित औपनिवेशिक रियायत के बीच का अंतर है।
hi.final_explanation:
अगस्त 1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा पहली बार स्पष्ट रूप से यह स्वीकार करना था कि भारत के लिए जिम्मेदार सरकार एक नीति लक्ष्य था। हालांकि, यह बहुत सीमित थी — उपयोग की गई अभिव्यक्ति 'स्वशासी संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास' थी, न कि तत्काल या डोमिनियन स्तर के स्वशासन का कोई वादा।

• कथन 1 — गलत: घोषणा में 'तत्काल' शब्द कहीं नहीं है। 'क्रमिक' शब्द मुख्य शर्त था, और राष्ट्रीयतावादियों ने इसे इसी कारण आलोचना की।
• कथन 2 — सही: एडविन मोंटागु भारत के सचिव थे। लॉर्ड चेल्म्सफोर्ड उस समय भारत के वायसराय थे — इनके पद अक्सर उलटफेर किए जाते हैं।
• कथन 3 — सही: मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट, जो संवैधानिक सुधारों की सिफारिश करती है, 1918 में प्रकाशित हुई। अधिनियम स्वयं 1919 में आया — तीन लगातार वर्षों में तीन अलग-अलग मील के पत्थर।

Value Addition:
• 1917 की घोषणा संवैधानिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण मानी जाती है क्योंकि यह पहली बार 'जिम्मेदार सरकार' को भारत के लिए ब्रिटिश उद्देश्य के रूप में स्पष्ट रूप से प्रस्तुत करती है।
• इसने डोमिनियन स्थिति का वादा नहीं किया — राष्ट्रीयतावादियों, विशेषकर एनी बेसेंट और तिलक, ने इसे बहुत ही संकोची पाया।
• मोंटागु-चेल्म्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट (1918) ने 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम की आधारशिला रखी, जिसे दिसंबर 1919 में रॉयल असेंट मिला।

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the bicameral central legislature created by the Government of India Act 1919:

1. The Council of State introduced under the Government of India Act 1919 had 145 members, of whom 105 were elected.
2. The introduction of bicameralism at the central level under the 1919 Act replaced the single-chamber Imperial Legislative Council that had existed under the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

Which of the above statement(s) is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 only
(c) Both 1 and 2
(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: The Council of State introduced under the Government of India Act 1919 had 145 members, of whom 105 were elected.
statement_analysis.reason: These figures belong to the Central Legislative Assembly, not the Council of State. The Council of State had 60 members, of whom 27 were elected — the numbers are commonly transposed.

statement_analysis.statement: The introduction of bicameralism at the central level under the 1919 Act replaced the single-chamber Imperial Legislative Council that had existed under the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
statement_analysis.reason: This is accurate — the Morley-Minto Act created a single Imperial Legislative Council, and the 1919 Act replaced it with a bicameral legislature consisting of the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly.

en.strong_distractor: b — Option b is deceptive because Statement 2 is entirely correct; students who assume the question asks for the incorrect statement may mistakenly mark Statement 1 as correct after recognising some of its numbers as genuine figures from the 1919 Act.
elimination_logic: Focus on Statement 1: 145 members and 105 elected — these are the correct figures for the Central Legislative Assembly, not the Council of State. The Council of State had 60 members (27 elected). Statement 1 is NOT correct.
Focus on Statement 2: The Morley-Minto 1909 Act created a single Imperial Legislative Council. The 1919 Act created a bicameral central legislature. Statement 2 is correct.
The question asks which statement is NOT correct — only Statement 1 fits that criterion.
Select option (a): 1 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap uses real numbers from the 1919 Act but assigns them to the wrong chamber. Both 60/27 (Council of State) and 145/105 (Legislative Assembly) are genuine figures — swapping them creates a plausible-sounding but factually incorrect statement. A student who recalls '105 elected members' without remembering which chamber will mark Statement 1 as correct.
en.final_explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919 introduced bicameralism at the Centre for the first time, creating a Council of State (Upper House) and a Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House).

• Statement 1 — NOT Correct: The figures 145 total members and 105 elected belong to the Central Legislative Assembly. The Council of State had 60 members, of whom only 27 were elected — the remainder were nominated. Swapping these figures is one of the most classic numerical traps in this topic.
• Statement 2 — Correct: The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909) had created a single Imperial Legislative Council. The 1919 Act abolished this and replaced it with a two-chamber structure at the Centre.

Value Addition:
• The Council of State (Upper House) was a more conservative body with higher property qualifications for both voters and candidates.
• Despite the elected majority in the Legislative Assembly, the Viceroy retained powers of certification and dissolution — diluting the legislature's real authority.
• The bicameral structure introduced in 1919 foreshadowed the Constituent Assembly's eventual adoption of a bicameral Parliament under the 1950 Constitution.

table_data.header_text: Consider the following statements about communal representation under the Government of India Act 1919:
rows: Muslims were granted separate electorates for the first time under the Government of India Act 1919.
The Government of India Act 1919 extended separate electorates to Sikhs.
Anglo-Indians received separate electoral representation under the Government of India Act 1919.
Scheduled Castes (Depressed Classes) were granted separate electorates under the Government of India Act 1919.
table_data.footer_text:
How many of the above statements are correct?

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three
(d) All four

statement_analysis.statement: Muslims were granted separate electorates for the first time under the Government of India Act 1919.
statement_analysis.reason: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by the Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909), not the 1919 Act — the 1919 Act extended them to additional communities.

statement_analysis.statement: The Government of India Act 1919 extended separate electorates to Sikhs.
statement_analysis.reason: Sikhs were among the communities to whom separate electorates were extended under the 1919 Act — they had not been covered under the 1909 provisions.

statement_analysis.statement: Anglo-Indians received separate electoral representation under the Government of India Act 1919.
statement_analysis.reason: Anglo-Indians were one of the new communities added to the communal representation framework by the 1919 Act.

statement_analysis.statement: Scheduled Castes (Depressed Classes) were granted separate electorates under the Government of India Act 1919.
statement_analysis.reason: Separate electorates for Depressed Classes came only with the Communal Award of 1932 — they were not included in the 1919 Act's communal representation framework.

en.strong_distractor: c — Option c (only three correct) tempts students who correctly recall Sikhs and Anglo-Indians but incorrectly also attribute the Muslim separate electorate to 1919, and then doubt Statement 4 but not Statement 1.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Separate electorates for Muslims originated in the Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto). The 1919 Act extended them to other communities. Statement 1 is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 2: Sikhs were added to the separate electorate system by the 1919 Act. Statement 2 is correct.
Evaluate Statement 3: Anglo-Indians were added under the 1919 Act. Statement 3 is correct.
Evaluate Statement 4: Depressed Classes / Scheduled Castes received separate electorates only under the Communal Award 1932, later modified by the Poona Pact. Statement 4 is incorrect.
Two statements correct (2 and 3) — select option (b): Only two.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: This question exploits two simultaneous traps: students confuse the origin of Muslim separate electorates (1909, not 1919) and also incorrectly believe Depressed Classes were included in 1919. Both errors push students toward overcounting. The real answer requires knowing not just what 1919 added, but what it did NOT add.
en.final_explanation:
The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced the principle of communal representation by creating separate electorates for Muslims. The Government of India Act 1919 did not create but extended this framework to additional communities.

| Statement | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Muslims granted separate electorates for first time under 1919 Act | Incorrect — introduced in 1909 |
| Sikhs granted separate electorates under 1919 Act | Correct |
| Anglo-Indians granted separate electorates under 1919 Act | Correct |
| Depressed Classes granted separate electorates under 1919 Act | Incorrect — came with Communal Award 1932 |

Value Addition:
• The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Europeans, Anglo-Indians, and Indian Christians — four new communities.
• The Communal Award (1932) proposed separate electorates for Depressed Classes, which Gandhi opposed through his fast-unto-death, leading to the Poona Pact (1932) — reserved seats in general electorates instead.
• The trajectory: 1909 (Muslims) → 1919 (extended) → 1932 (Communal Award) → 1932 Poona Pact → 1935 Act's elaboration of reservations.

hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प c (केवल तीन सही) उन छात्रों को भ्रमित करता है जो सही रूप से सिखों और एंग्लो-इंडियनों को याद करते हैं लेकिन मुसलमानों के पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल को 1919 से जोड़ते हैं, और फिर कथन 4 पर संदेह करते हैं पर कथन 1 पर नहीं।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 का मूल्यांकन करें: मुसलमानों के लिए पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto) में शुरू हुए थे। 1919 के अधिनियम ने इन्हें अन्य समुदायों तक बढ़ाया। अतः कथन 1 गलत है।
कथन 2 का मूल्यांकन करें: सिखों को 1919 के अधिनियम द्वारा पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल प्रणाली में जोड़ा गया। अतः कथन 2 सही है।
कथन 3 का मूल्यांकन करें: एंग्लो-इंडियनों को 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत जोड़ा गया। अतः कथन 3 सही है।
कथन 4 का मूल्यांकन करें: अल्पसंख्यक जातियों / अनुसूचित जातियों को पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल केवल 1932 के Communal Award के तहत मिले, जिसे बाद में पूना समझौते द्वारा संशोधित किया गया। अतः कथन 4 गलत है।
दो कथन सही हैं (2 और 3) — विकल्प (b) चुनें: केवल दो।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह प्रश्न दो समवर्ती जालों का उपयोग करता है: छात्र मुसलमानों के पृथक निर्वाचन मंडलों की उत्पत्ति (1909, 1919 नहीं) को भ्रमित करते हैं और साथ ही गलत रूप से मानते हैं कि अनुसूचित जातियाँ 1919 में शामिल थीं। दोनों त्रुटियाँ छात्रों को अधिक गिनती की ओर ले जाती हैं। सही उत्तर जानने के लिए यह आवश्यक है कि केवल 1919 में जोड़ा गया क्या था, और क्या नहीं था।
hi.final_explanation:
मोर्ले-मिंटो सुधारों 1909 ने मुसलमानों के लिए पृथक निर्वाचन मंडलों की अवधारणा प्रस्तुत की। भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 ने इस ढांचे को नया नहीं बनाया बल्कि अतिरिक्त समुदायों तक बढ़ाया।

| कथन | निर्णय |
|---|---|
| मुसलमानों को पहली बार 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल मिले | गलत — 1909 में शुरू हुए |
| सिखों को 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल मिले | सही |
| एंग्लो-इंडियनों को 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल मिले | सही |
| अनुसूचित जातियों को 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल मिले | गलत — 1932 के Communal Award के साथ आए |

मूल्य वर्धन:
• 1919 के अधिनियम ने सिखों, यूरोपियों, एंग्लो-इंडियनों और भारतीय ईसाइयों को सामुदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व में जोड़ा — चार नए समुदाय।
• Communal Award (1932) ने अनुसूचित जातियों के लिए पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल प्रस्तावित किए, जिनका गांधी ने उपवास के माध्यम से विरोध किया, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप पूना समझौता (1932) हुआ — जिसमें सामान्य निर्वाचन मंडलों में आरक्षित सीटें दी गईं।
• क्रम: 1909 (मुसलमान) → 1919 (विस्तार) → 1932 (Communal Award) → 1932 पूना समझौता → 1935 अधिनियम में आरक्षण का विस्तार।

Eliminate option (a): The 1919 Act did NOT grant universal women's franchise. Women's franchise was left to provincial discretion — it was not a uniform central provision.
Eliminate option (b): The Montagu Declaration (1917) was a policy statement, not a legislative instrument that could operationalize voting rights.
Confirm option (c): The 1919 Act left women's suffrage to the discretion of each province. Madras was the first province to exercise that discretion and grant women the right to vote in 1921.

Eliminate option (d): The Devolution Rules 1920 divided subjects into categories but did not specifically address women's franchise — this was a provincial legislature decision, not a devolution rule provision.

In reality, women's franchise was deliberately left ambiguous — provincial governments could choose. Students who recall 'Madras granted women the vote first' without knowing the legal mechanism (provincial discretion under the Act) frequently select wrong options about uniform central grant.
en.final_explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919 expanded the franchise significantly from the Morley-Minto era — approximately 10% of the population was enfranchised — but the Act deliberately left women's franchise to the discretion of individual provinces rather than mandating it centrally.

Applicable principle: Women's franchise under the 1919 Act was a matter of provincial legislative discretion. The Act itself contained no universal provision granting women the right to vote. Each provincial council was empowered to decide independently.

Mapping to the scenario: When a provincial council granted women voting rights after 1919, it was exercising the discretionary authority the Act permitted, not implementing a centrally mandated provision.

• Option (a): Incorrect — the 1919 Act established no uniform women's franchise; the Act left it to provinces.
• Option (b): Incorrect — the Montagu Declaration was a political statement, not an operative legal instrument on franchise.
• Option (c): Correct — Madras was the first province to grant women voting rights in 1921, exercising the discretion the Act conferred on provinces.
• Option (d): Incorrect — the Devolution Rules dealt with division of subjects between reserved and transferred categories, not with franchise criteria.

Value Addition:
• Madras (1921) was followed by other provinces in gradually extending women's franchise.
• Universal adult franchise — for both men and women — arrived only with the Constitution of India in 1950.
• The 1935 Act increased franchise to approximately 14% of the population but still did not provide universal suffrage.

en.display_text:
Three of the following four statements about the genesis of the Central Public Service Commission are consistent with established historical facts. Which one does NOT belong with the others?

(a) The Government of India Act 1919 provided the first statutory basis for a Public Service Commission at the Centre.
(b) The Central Public Service Commission came into existence immediately upon the Government of India Act 1919 coming into force.
(c) The Lee Commission of 1924 recommended the establishment of the Central Public Service Commission and accelerated its creation.
(d) The Federal Public Service Commission under the 1935 Act and the eventual Union Public Service Commission under the 1950 Constitution were the institutional successors of the body established in this period.
en.strong_distractor: d — Option d is deceptive because UPSC (post-1950) is the most familiar form of the public service commission; students who know it was created under the 1950 Constitution may doubt whether the 1935 Act established a distinct body.
elimination_logic: The question asks which statement about the Central Public Service Commission does NOT belong with the others — i.e., which is factually incorrect.
Evaluate option (a): The 1919 Act provided the first statutory basis for a Public Service Commission at the Centre — correct.

Evaluate option (b): The Central Public Service Commission was established in 1919 immediately upon the Act's passage — INCORRECT. The Act provided for it in 1919, but actual establishment occurred in 1926 after the Lee Commission (1924) recommendation. This is the odd one out.
Evaluate option (c): The Lee Commission of 1924 recommended the establishment of the Commission and accelerated its creation — correct.
Evaluate option (d): The Federal Public Service Commission under the 1935 Act and the eventual UPSC under the 1950 Constitution are the successors — correct trajectory.
Option (b) is the incorrect claim — select (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The gap between the statutory provision (1919) and actual establishment (1926) is a classic UPSC trap. Students who recall '1919 Act created the Public Service Commission' collapse the provision and the implementation into one event, arriving at the wrong year. The Lee Commission's 1924 recommendation was the trigger that led to the 1926 establishment.
en.final_explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919 provided the statutory basis for a Public Service Commission at the Centre — but this was a provision, not an implementation. The actual body was established seven years later.

• Option (a): Correct — the 1919 Act was the first to provide statutory authority for a central Public Service Commission.
• Option (b): Incorrect — the Central Public Service Commission was NOT established immediately in 1919. It was established in 1926, following the Lee Commission's 1924 recommendation. This is the odd one out.
• Option (c): Correct — the Royal Commission on the Superior Civil Services in India (Lee Commission, 1924) specifically recommended the Commission's establishment to Indianize services systematically.
• Option (d): Correct — the evolution ran from the 1919 provision → 1926 establishment → Federal Public Service Commission under 1935 → UPSC under the 1950 Constitution.

Value Addition:
• The Lee Commission (1924) also recommended a 50:50 ratio of British and Indian recruits to the ICS over a 15-year period.
• The first Public Service Commission (1926) was chaired by Sir Ross Barker.
• The 1950 Constitution's UPSC is a constitutionally established body under Article 315, distinct from its statutory predecessor.

hi.final_explanation:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 ने केंद्र में सार्वजनिक सेवा आयोग के लिए वैधानिक आधार प्रदान किया — लेकिन यह केवल एक प्रावधान था, क्रियान्वयन नहीं। वास्तविक निकाय सात वर्ष बाद स्थापित हुआ।

• विकल्प (a): सही — 1919 का अधिनियम केंद्र में सार्वजनिक सेवा आयोग के लिए पहला वैधानिक प्राधिकार प्रदान करता है।
• विकल्प (b): गलत — केंद्रीय सार्वजनिक सेवा आयोग 1919 में तुरंत स्थापित नहीं हुआ था। यह 1926 में स्थापित हुआ, ली आयोग की 1924 की सिफारिश के बाद। यह असामान्य विकल्प है।
• विकल्प (c): सही — भारत में उच्च नागरिक सेवाओं पर रॉयल कमीशन (ली आयोग, 1924) ने विशेष रूप से आयोग की स्थापना की सिफारिश की ताकि सेवाओं का भारतीयकरण व्यवस्थित हो सके।
• विकल्प (d): सही — विकास क्रम था: 1919 का प्रावधान → 1926 की स्थापना → 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत संघीय सार्वजनिक सेवा आयोग → 1950 के संविधान के तहत UPSC।

Statement 2: Despite the 1919 Act's transfer of the Secretary of State's salary to the British Exchequer, his superintendence, direction, and control over the Government of India remained substantively intact.

Which one of the following is correct?

(a) Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
(b) Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are incorrect
(c) Statement 1 is incorrect but Statement 2 is correct
(d) Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is incorrect

statement_analysis.statement: Prior to the Government of India Act 1919, the salary of the Secretary of State for India was charged to British Exchequer revenues, and the 1919 Act transferred this cost to Indian revenues.
statement_analysis.reason: This is the reverse of the actual change. Pre-1919, the Secretary of State's salary was paid from Indian revenues — a nationalist grievance. The 1919 Act transferred this cost to the British Exchequer, not the other way around.

statement_analysis.statement: Despite the 1919 Act's transfer of the Secretary of State's salary to the British Exchequer, his superintendence, direction, and control over the Government of India remained substantively intact.
statement_analysis.reason: The salary change was symbolic — the Secretary of State retained full authority over India's governance. The 1919 Act did not meaningfully curtail his powers of superintendence and control.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (both correct) is deceptive because Statement 2 is accurate, and students who are uncertain about the direction of the salary change in Statement 1 may assume both are correct.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Pre-1919, the Secretary of State's salary came from Indian revenues. The 1919 Act moved it to the British Exchequer. Statement 1 describes the opposite — it is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 2: The salary shift was symbolic; superintendence and direction remained intact. Statement 2 is correct.
Statement 1 incorrect + Statement 2 correct — select option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 1 uses a reversal trap: by describing the pre-1919 situation as 'British Exchequer funded' and the Act as moving it to 'Indian revenues,' it inverts the actual reform. Students who know there was a change in the salary arrangement but not its direction will mark Statement 1 as correct.
en.final_explanation:
The Secretary of State for India's salary was a longstanding nationalist grievance: Indians were effectively paying the salary of the official who governed them on behalf of Britain. The Government of India Act 1919 corrected this — shifting the Secretary of State's salary to the British Exchequer — as a symbolic concession.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: The statement reverses the historical reality. Pre-1919: Indian revenues paid the salary. Post-1919: British Exchequer paid it. The claim that 1919 moved costs to Indian revenues is factually backward.
• Statement 2 — Correct: The salary transfer was symbolic. The Secretary of State retained superintendence, direction, and control over Indian affairs — his actual powers were not diminished by the financial adjustment.

Value Addition:
• The India Council in London (created 1858) was retained under 1919, but its mandatory consultation powers were reduced — size cut from 15 to 8–12 members.
• The India Council was finally abolished under the Government of India Act 1935.
• The salary grievance was one of many 'drain of wealth' arguments used by Dadabhai Naoroji and other economic nationalists.

hi.final_explanation:
भारत के सचिव का वेतन एक पुरानी राष्ट्रवादी शिकायत थी: भारतीय प्रभावी रूप से उस अधिकारी का वेतन दे रहे थे जो ब्रिटेन की ओर से उन्हें शासित करता था। भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 ने इसे ठीक किया — सचिव के वेतन को ब्रिटिश खजाने पर स्थानांतरित कर एक प्रतीकात्मक रियायत दी।

en.display_text:
Which of the following pairs relating to the political context of the Government of India Act 1919 is correctly matched?

(a) Rowlatt Act : passed in March 1919, preceding the Government of India Act passed in December 1919
(b) Swarajist reversal of the council boycott : 1922, at the Gaya session of the Indian National Congress
(c) Non-Cooperation Movement formally launched : 1919, immediately following the passage of the Government of India Act
(d) Gandhi's formal endorsement of the 1919 reforms : February 1920, after initial hesitation
en.strong_distractor: b — Option b is deceptive because students who recall the Swarajist reversal of the council boycott associate it with 1921 or 1922, not 1923, and may also incorrectly link it to the Non-Cooperation Movement's formal launch.
elimination_logic: The question asks for the correctly matched pair — evaluate each option.
Evaluate option (a): Rowlatt Act — March 1919; Government of India Act — December 1919. Both in 1919, Rowlatt preceding. This is correct.
Evaluate option (b): The Swarajist reversal of council boycott occurred in 1923, not 1922. Incorrect pairing.
Evaluate option (c): Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920 (not 1919), after the Nagpur Congress session. Incorrect pairing.

Evaluate option (d): Gandhi's assessment of the reforms as insufficient was stated in 1920 — but attributing his formal opposition to the Rowlatt Act 1919 as the primary trigger for Non-Cooperation (which began in 1920 over multiple factors) is an oversimplification that makes this pairing inexact.
Only option (a) presents a correctly matched factual pair — select (a).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal trap lies in students conflating all 1919 events into a single undifferentiated year. The critical distinction is that the Rowlatt Act (March 1919) and the Government of India Act (December 1919) were passed in the same calendar year, with repression preceding reform — but many students reverse their sequence or assume they were simultaneous.
en.final_explanation:
1919 was a year of simultaneous legislative contradiction: the British government passed both a repressive act and a reform act within the same year.

• Option (a): Correct — the Rowlatt Act was passed in March 1919, the Government of India Act in December 1919. Both within the same year, with repression preceding reform. This is the correctly matched pair.
• Option (b): Incorrect — the Swarajist faction's decision to enter councils occurred at the special Congress session of 1923, not 1922.
• Option (c): Incorrect — the Non-Cooperation Movement was formally launched in 1920, following the Nagpur Congress session. It was not launched in 1919.
• Option (d): Incorrect as stated — while Gandhi was critical of the reforms, the Non-Cooperation Movement's formal launch in 1920 was triggered by multiple factors including Khilafat, Jallianwala Bagh, and the inadequacy of the 1919 Act.

Value Addition:
• The Rowlatt Act allowed detention without trial — it was the immediate trigger for Jallianwala Bagh (April 1919).
• Congress initially boycotted the reformed councils under Non-Cooperation (1920) but the Swarajists under C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru reversed this in 1923 to 'obstruct from within.'
• The coexistence of reform and repression in 1919 is a key analytical theme for UPSC mains as well.

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the Devolution Rules 1920 that operationalized the dyarchy system:

1. The Government of India Act 1919 itself contained an exhaustive list of all reserved and transferred subjects for each province, making the Devolution Rules 1920 merely procedural in nature.
2. The Devolution Rules 1920 vested the Governor with a power to restore a transferred subject to the reserved category, making the transferred classification reversible.
3. Finance was categorized as a reserved subject under the Devolution Rules 1920, effectively limiting elected ministers' capacity to administer their transferred subjects.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 1 only
(d) 2 and 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: The Government of India Act 1919 itself contained an exhaustive list of all reserved and transferred subjects for each province, making the Devolution Rules 1920 merely procedural in nature.
statement_analysis.reason: The Act did not enumerate all subjects — the actual division into central, provincial-reserved, and provincial-transferred categories was effected through the subsidiary Devolution Rules 1920. The Rules were substantive, not merely procedural.

statement_analysis.statement: The Devolution Rules 1920 vested the Governor with a power to restore a transferred subject to the reserved category, making the transferred classification reversible.
statement_analysis.reason: The 'takeback' provision allowed the Governor to revert a transferred subject to reserved status — this provision was one of the core structural weaknesses critics identified in the dyarchy framework.

statement_analysis.statement: Finance was categorized as a reserved subject under the Devolution Rules 1920, effectively limiting elected ministers' capacity to administer their transferred subjects.
statement_analysis.reason: Finance remained reserved, meaning elected ministers responsible for transferred subjects like education and public health had no independent financial authority — the central critique of dyarchy as 'unworkable.'

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is the strong distractor here — wait, correct answer is (d) meaning 2 and 3 only. The strong distractor is option (a) which includes Statement 1 as correct.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: The 1919 Act did NOT list all subjects — the Devolution Rules 1920 performed this function and were substantively important. Statement 1 is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 2: The 'takeback' provision allowing restoration of transferred to reserved status was indeed in the Devolution Rules — Statement 2 is correct.
Evaluate Statement 3: Finance was reserved, crippling the transferred ministers — this is factually accurate. Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct — select option (d): 2 and 3 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 1 exploits the assumption that parent legislation always contains the substantive classifications. In the 1919 framework, the Act created the dyarchy structure but delegated the actual subject-classification to subsidiary Devolution Rules — a distinction that matters for understanding how British colonial legislation worked through executive instruments rather than direct statutory enumeration.
en.final_explanation:
The Devolution Rules 1920 were the operative instruments that gave dyarchy its content. Without them, the 1919 Act's dyarchy provisions would have been a structure without substance.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: The 1919 Act established the framework but left the enumeration of subjects to the Devolution Rules. This was deliberate — it allowed flexibility without amending the Act. The Rules were substantive, not procedural.
• Statement 2 — Correct: The Governor's power to 'take back' a transferred subject to reserved status meant no transferred subject was permanently beyond executive reassertion. This undermined ministerial security and made dyarchy inherently fragile.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Retention of finance under the reserved category was the fatal flaw critics (including Montagu himself, later) acknowledged. Elected ministers administering education or public health had to beg the Governor's Executive Council for funds.

Value Addition:
• The Devolution Rules conceptually preceded the more elaborate three-list system (Federal, Provincial, Concurrent) under the 1935 Act.
• Provincial autonomy under the 1935 Act eliminated the reserved/transferred distinction in provinces entirely.
• The dyarchy critique 'transferred ministers, reserved finance' became a stock phrase in the Indian political vocabulary of the 1920s.

hi.display_text:
द्विध्रुवीय शासन प्रणाली को लागू करने वाले Devolution Rules 1920 के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

1. Government of India Act 1919 में प्रत्येक प्रांत के लिए सभी आरक्षित और स्थानांतरित विषयों की एक विस्तृत सूची शामिल थी, जिससे Devolution Rules 1920 केवल प्रक्रियात्मक प्रकृति के थे।
2. Devolution Rules 1920 ने गवर्नर को स्थानांतरित विषय को आरक्षित श्रेणी में पुनः स्थापित करने का अधिकार दिया, जिससे स्थानांतरित वर्गीकरण उलटने योग्य हो गया।
3. वित्त को Devolution Rules 1920 के तहत एक आरक्षित विषय के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया था, जिससे निर्वाचित मंत्रियों की अपनी स्थानांतरित विषयों को प्रशासन करने की क्षमता प्रभावी रूप से सीमित हो गई।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1 और 2
(b) केवल 1 और 3
(c) केवल 1
(d) केवल 2 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Government of India Act 1919 itself contained an exhaustive list of all reserved and transferred subjects for each province, making the Devolution Rules 1920 merely procedural in nature.
statement_analysis.reason: अधिनियम ने सभी विषयों की सूची नहीं दी — केंद्रीय, प्रांतीय-आरक्षित, और प्रांतीय-स्थानांतरित वर्गीकरण वास्तव में सहायक Devolution Rules 1920 के माध्यम से किया गया था। ये नियम केवल प्रक्रियात्मक नहीं बल्कि सारगर्भित थे।

statement_analysis.statement: The Devolution Rules 1920 vested the Governor with a power to restore a transferred subject to the reserved category, making the transferred classification reversible.
statement_analysis.reason: 'टेकबैक' प्रावधान ने गवर्नर को स्थानांतरित विषय को आरक्षित श्रेणी में वापस लाने का अधिकार दिया — यह प्रावधान द्विध्रुवीय शासन (dyarchy) के ढांचे में आलोचकों द्वारा पहचानी गई मुख्य संरचनात्मक कमजोरियों में से एक था।

statement_analysis.statement: Finance was categorized as a reserved subject under the Devolution Rules 1920, effectively limiting elected ministers' capacity to administer their transferred subjects.
statement_analysis.reason: वित्त को आरक्षित विषय के रूप में रखा गया था, जिसका अर्थ है कि शिक्षा और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य जैसे स्थानांतरित विषयों के लिए जिम्मेदार निर्वाचित मंत्रियों के पास स्वतंत्र वित्तीय अधिकार नहीं था — यह द्विध्रुवीय शासन की 'अकार्यशीलता' की केंद्रीय आलोचना थी।

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (सभी तीन सही) यहाँ मजबूत भ्रम पैदा करता है — ध्यान दें, सही उत्तर (d) है जिसका अर्थ है केवल 2 और 3 सही हैं। मजबूत भ्रम विकल्प (a) है जिसमें कथन 1 को भी सही माना गया है।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 का मूल्यांकन करें: 1919 का अधिनियम सभी विषयों की सूची नहीं देता — Devolution Rules 1920 ने यह कार्य किया और ये नियम सारगर्भित थे। अतः कथन 1 गलत है।
कथन 2 का मूल्यांकन करें: 'टेकबैक' प्रावधान जो स्थानांतरित विषय को आरक्षित में वापस लाने की अनुमति देता है, वास्तव में Devolution Rules में था — अतः कथन 2 सही है।
कथन 3 का मूल्यांकन करें: वित्त आरक्षित था, जिससे स्थानांतरित मंत्रियों की क्षमता सीमित हुई — यह तथ्यात्मक रूप से सही है। अतः कथन 3 सही है।
कथन 2 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (d) चुनें: केवल 2 और 3।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 1 इस धारणा का उपयोग करता है कि मूल विधेयक में हमेशा सारगर्भित वर्गीकरण होते हैं। 1919 के ढांचे में, अधिनियम ने द्विध्रुवीय शासन की संरचना बनाई लेकिन विषय-वर्गीकरण सहायक Devolution Rules को सौंप दिया — यह अंतर समझना आवश्यक है कि ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक विधायिका कार्यकारी उपकरणों के माध्यम से कैसे काम करती थी, न कि सीधे सांविधिक सूचीकरण के द्वारा।
hi.final_explanation:
Devolution Rules 1920 वे कार्यकारी उपकरण थे जिन्होंने द्विध्रुवीय शासन को उसका वास्तविक स्वरूप दिया। इनके बिना, 1919 अधिनियम के द्विध्रुवीय प्रावधान केवल एक बिना सार की संरचना होते।

• कथन 1 — गलत: 1919 अधिनियम ने ढांचा स्थापित किया लेकिन विषयों की सूची Devolution Rules को छोड़ दी। यह जानबूझकर किया गया था — जिससे अधिनियम में संशोधन किए बिना लचीलापन बना रहे। ये नियम सारगर्भित थे, केवल प्रक्रियात्मक नहीं।
• कथन 2 — सही: गवर्नर की वह शक्ति कि वह स्थानांतरित विषय को आरक्षित में वापस ले सकता है, इसका अर्थ था कि कोई भी स्थानांतरित विषय स्थायी रूप से कार्यकारी पुनः दावा से बाहर नहीं था। इससे मंत्री सुरक्षा कमजोर हुई और द्विध्रुवीय शासन स्वाभाविक रूप से अस्थिर बन गया।
• कथन 3 — सही: वित्त को आरक्षित श्रेणी में रखना वह घातक दोष था जिसे आलोचकों (जिसमें बाद में मोंटागु स्वयं भी शामिल थे) ने स्वीकार किया। शिक्षा या सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य के लिए जिम्मेदार निर्वाचित मंत्रियों को गवर्नर के कार्यकारी परिषद से धन की भीख माँगनी पड़ती थी।

Value Addition:
• Devolution Rules ने 1935 अधिनियम के तीन-सूची प्रणाली (संघीय, प्रांतीय, समवर्ती) से पहले अवधारणात्मक रूप से मार्ग प्रशस्त किया।
• 1935 अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता ने प्रांतों में आरक्षित/स्थानांतरित भेद को पूरी तरह समाप्त कर दिया।
• द्विध्रुवीय शासन की आलोचना 'स्थानांतरित मंत्री, आरक्षित वित्त' 1920 के दशक के भारतीय राजनीतिक शब्दावली में एक स्थायी वाक्यांश बन गई।

shared.concept_anchor: Viceroy's certification and non-votable budget provisions under 1919 Act

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Viceroy and the financial provisions under the Government of India Act 1919:

1. The Viceroy under the Government of India Act 1919 could certify a bill that the Central Legislative Assembly had refused to pass, thereby enacting it without legislative approval.
2. The entire budget under the Government of India Act 1919 was subject to vote in the Central Legislative Assembly, giving elected members full financial control over government expenditure.
3. The Viceroy's power to issue ordinances under the 1919 Act required prior approval from the Council of State before taking effect.

Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Viceroy under the Government of India Act 1919 could certify a bill that the Central Legislative Assembly had refused to pass, thereby enacting it without legislative approval.
statement_analysis.reason: The certification power was real — if the legislature refused a bill the Viceroy considered essential, he could certify it and it became law, effectively nullifying the legislature's vote.

statement_analysis.statement: The entire budget under the Government of India Act 1919 was subject to vote in the Central Legislative Assembly, giving elected members full financial control over government expenditure.
statement_analysis.reason: A significant portion of the budget was classified as 'non-votable' — not subject to the Assembly's vote. Financial control remained restricted, and elected members could not exercise complete budgetary authority.

statement_analysis.statement: The Viceroy's power to issue ordinances under the 1919 Act required prior approval from the Council of State before taking effect.
statement_analysis.reason: Ordinances did not require prior legislative approval — they were an executive instrument to bypass the legislature entirely. This was one of the mechanisms that made the legislature's sovereignty illusory.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (Statement 1 only not correct) is deceptive because the certification power sounds like it should be unconstitutional, leading students to doubt Statement 1 — but it was a genuine power explicitly provided in the Act.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Certification power was explicitly provided in the 1919 Act — the Viceroy could enact refused bills. Statement 1 is CORRECT, so it does not satisfy 'NOT correct.'
Evaluate Statement 2: The budget was split — a non-votable portion existed, meaning elected members did NOT have full financial control. Statement 2 is NOT correct.
Evaluate Statement 3: Ordinances required no prior Council of State approval — this is an invented procedural requirement. Statement 3 is NOT correct.
Statements 2 and 3 are NOT correct — select option (c): 2 and 3 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses a 'scope-extension' trap by claiming the entire budget was votable. Students who recall that elected members had some financial role may not recall the critical 'non-votable' portion distinction. The false claim of 'full financial control' is what makes this a trap — partial truth extended to a false totality.
en.final_explanation:
The Viceroy's retained powers under the 1919 Act fundamentally compromised the legislature's authority, despite the expansion of elected representation.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Certification was a real and exercised power. If the Viceroy certified a refused bill as essential to India's safety or tranquility, it became law regardless of the vote — a blunt overriding instrument.
• Statement 2 — NOT Correct: The budget was divided into votable and non-votable sections. A substantial portion of government expenditure fell into the non-votable category — for instance, defence spending and certain obligatory charges. 'Full financial control' was never achieved.
• Statement 3 — NOT Correct: Ordinances (Section 72 power) were purely executive and did not require any prior legislative sanction from either house. The ordinance power was specifically designed to operate independently of the legislature.

Value Addition:
• The non-votable budget provision was a direct parallel to the 'charged expenditure' concept in the Westminster system, but applied far more broadly in colonial India.
• The Viceroy's certification power was criticised as making the legislature a 'debating society' with no real authority.
• The Westminster model the British claimed to be moving India toward had no equivalent to these retained executive overrides.

hi.display_text:
1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय के अधिकारों और वित्तीय प्रावधानों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

1. 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय उस विधेयक को प्रमाणित कर सकता था जिसे केंद्रीय विधायी सभा ने पारित करने से इनकार कर दिया था, इस प्रकार उसे विधायी अनुमोदन के बिना लागू कर देता था।
2. 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत पूरा बजट केंद्रीय विधायी सभा में मतदान के अधीन था, जिससे निर्वाचित सदस्यों को सरकारी व्यय पर पूर्ण वित्तीय नियंत्रण प्राप्त था।
3. 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय को अध्यादेश जारी करने के लिए राज्य परिषद की पूर्व स्वीकृति आवश्यक थी।

उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही नहीं है/हैं?

(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 1 और 3
(c) केवल 2 और 3
(d) 1, 2 और 3

statement_analysis.statement: 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय उस विधेयक को प्रमाणित कर सकता था जिसे केंद्रीय विधायी सभा ने पारित करने से इनकार कर दिया था, इस प्रकार उसे विधायी अनुमोदन के बिना लागू कर देता था।
statement_analysis.reason: प्रमाणीकरण शक्ति वास्तविक थी — यदि विधायिका ने किसी विधेयक को अस्वीकार कर दिया जिसे वाइसराय आवश्यक समझता था, तो वह उसे प्रमाणित कर सकता था और वह कानून बन जाता था, जिससे विधायिका के मतदान का प्रभाव समाप्त हो जाता था।

statement_analysis.statement: 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत पूरा बजट केंद्रीय विधायी सभा में मतदान के अधीन था, जिससे निर्वाचित सदस्यों को सरकारी व्यय पर पूर्ण वित्तीय नियंत्रण प्राप्त था।
statement_analysis.reason: बजट का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा 'गैर-मतदानीय' वर्गीकृत था — जो सभा के मतदान के अधीन नहीं था। वित्तीय नियंत्रण सीमित था, और निर्वाचित सदस्य पूर्ण बजटीय अधिकार नहीं रख सकते थे।

statement_analysis.statement: 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय को अध्यादेश जारी करने के लिए राज्य परिषद की पूर्व स्वीकृति आवश्यक थी।
statement_analysis.reason: अध्यादेशों को पूर्व विधायी स्वीकृति की आवश्यकता नहीं थी — वे पूरी तरह से कार्यकारी उपकरण थे जो विधायिका को पूरी तरह से दरकिनार कर देते थे। यह विधायिका की संप्रभुता को काल्पनिक बनाने वाले तंत्रों में से एक था।

hi.strong_distractor: (a) — विकल्प (a) (केवल कथन 1 सही नहीं है) भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि प्रमाणन शक्ति असंवैधानिक लगती है, जिससे छात्र कथन 1 पर संदेह करते हैं — लेकिन यह अधिनियम में स्पष्ट रूप से प्रदान की गई वास्तविक शक्ति थी।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 का मूल्यांकन करें: प्रमाणन शक्ति 1919 के अधिनियम में स्पष्ट रूप से प्रदान की गई थी — वाइसराय अस्वीकृत विधेयकों को लागू कर सकता था। कथन 1 सही है, अतः यह 'सही नहीं है' की शर्त पूरी नहीं करता।
कथन 2 का मूल्यांकन करें: बजट विभाजित था — एक गैर-मतदानीय हिस्सा था, जिसका अर्थ है कि निर्वाचित सदस्यों के पास पूर्ण वित्तीय नियंत्रण नहीं था। कथन 2 सही नहीं है।
कथन 3 का मूल्यांकन करें: अध्यादेशों के लिए राज्य परिषद की पूर्व स्वीकृति आवश्यक नहीं थी — यह एक काल्पनिक प्रक्रिया है। कथन 3 सही नहीं है।
अतः कथन 2 और 3 सही नहीं हैं — विकल्प (c) चुनें: केवल 2 और 3।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 में 'स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन' जाल है क्योंकि यह दावा करता है कि पूरा बजट मतदान योग्य था। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि निर्वाचित सदस्यों की कुछ वित्तीय भूमिका थी, वे 'गैर-मतदानीय' हिस्से के महत्वपूर्ण भेद को याद नहीं कर पाते। 'पूर्ण वित्तीय नियंत्रण' का गलत दावा ही इस जाल का कारण है — आंशिक सत्य को पूरी तरह गलत बताया गया है।
hi.final_explanation:
1919 के अधिनियम के तहत वाइसराय के बनाए गए अधिकारों ने निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधित्व के विस्तार के बावजूद विधायिका के अधिकार को मौलिक रूप से कमजोर कर दिया।

• कथन 1 — सही: प्रमाणन एक वास्तविक और प्रयुक्त शक्ति थी। यदि वाइसराय ने किसी अस्वीकृत विधेयक को भारत की सुरक्षा या शांति के लिए आवश्यक माना, तो वह उसे कानून बना देता था, चाहे मतदान कुछ भी हो — यह एक कठोर अधिमान्य उपकरण था।
• कथन 2 — सही नहीं: बजट को मतदान योग्य और गैर-मतदान योग्य भागों में विभाजित किया गया था। सरकारी व्यय का एक बड़ा हिस्सा गैर-मतदान योग्य था — जैसे रक्षा व्यय और कुछ अनिवार्य शुल्क। 'पूर्ण वित्तीय नियंत्रण' कभी प्राप्त नहीं हुआ।
• कथन 3 — सही नहीं: अध्यादेश (धारा 72 की शक्ति) पूरी तरह से कार्यकारी थे और किसी भी सदन से पूर्व विधायी स्वीकृति की आवश्यकता नहीं थी। अध्यादेश शक्ति विशेष रूप से विधायिका से स्वतंत्र रूप से संचालित होने के लिए डिज़ाइन की गई थी।

Value Addition:
• गैर-मतदान योग्य बजट प्रावधान वेस्टमिंस्टर प्रणाली के 'चार्ज्ड व्यय' की अवधारणा के समान था, लेकिन उपनिवेशी भारत में कहीं अधिक व्यापक रूप से लागू था।
• वाइसराय की प्रमाणन शक्ति की आलोचना इस आधार पर हुई कि इससे विधायिका केवल एक 'बहस करने वाला समाज' बन गई जिसका कोई वास्तविक अधिकार नहीं था।
• ब्रिटिश द्वारा भारत को वेस्टमिंस्टर मॉडल की ओर ले जाने का दावा किया गया था, जिसमें इन कार्यकारी अधिमान्यताओं के समान कोई व्यवस्था नहीं थी।

en.display_text:
Regarding the Indian National Congress's engagement with the reformed councils established under the Government of India Act 1919, which of the following statements is correct?

(a) The Swarajist faction secured Congress approval for council entry at the Gaya session (1922), after which C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru led the boycott reversal.
(b) After initial boycott under the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Swarajist faction reversed Congress policy in 1923, entering the reformed councils with the explicit strategy of obstructing the government from within.
(c) The Swarajist faction, unlike the Moderates, refused to enter the councils throughout the 1920s, maintaining the Non-Cooperation boycott until the Simon Commission was announced.
(d) C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru adopted a 'responsive cooperation' strategy in 1923, agreeing to constructively participate in the council proceedings rather than obstruct them.
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a is deceptive because C.R. Das is associated with the Swarajist faction, but attributing the 1923 Swarajist strategy specifically to 'the Gaya Congress session' (where C.R. Das resigned as Congress president after his council-entry resolution was defeated) confuses the event with the outcome.
elimination_logic: Identify the Swarajist strategy: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru proposed entering the reformed councils to obstruct the government from within — a departure from the Non-Cooperation boycott.
Eliminate option (a): The Swarajists did not get approval at the Gaya Congress (1922) — their resolution was defeated there, which led C.R. Das to resign as Congress president.
Confirm option (b): The Swarajists formed a separate political organization and won the reversal of the boycott decision in 1923, entering the councils after the elections of that year.
Eliminate option (c): The Moderates (Liberal Federation) — not the Swarajists — participated from the beginning. The Swarajists reversed the boycott in 1923.

Eliminate option (d): 'Responsive cooperation' was a distinct position adopted by some moderate nationalists; the Swarajist strategy was specifically 'obstruction from within' — different terminology and different intent.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The scope-extension trap involves conflating the Gaya Congress (1922) — where Swarajists lost the vote — with the 1923 reversal. Students who know C.R. Das and Gaya are associated may mark option (a) as correct without knowing that Gaya was the defeat, not the victory. The Swarajist reversal came later at the special Congress session and through separate political organization.
en.final_explanation:
The Non-Cooperation Movement's boycott of reformed councils posed a strategic dilemma after the movement was suspended following the Chauri Chaura incident (1922). The Swarajist faction under C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru argued for reversing the boycott and entering the councils to 'wreck the reforms from within.'

• Option (a): Incorrect — at the Gaya Congress session (1922), the Swarajist resolution for council entry was defeated. C.R. Das resigned the Congress presidency in frustration. The reversal came in 1923, not at Gaya.
• Option (b): Correct — in 1923, after winning sufficient support, the Swarajists entered the reformed councils. Their strategy was to obstruct government functioning from within the legislature, not to cooperate with it.
• Option (c): Incorrect — it was the Moderates (later Liberal Federation) who participated from the start, welcoming the reforms. The Swarajists joined only in 1923 after the Non-Cooperation boycott ended.
• Option (d): Incorrect — 'responsive cooperation' was associated with different moderate nationalists; the Swarajist strategy was explicitly described as 'obstruction from within,' not cooperation.

Value Addition:
• The Swarajists won significant seats in the 1923 elections and effectively paralysed council proceedings in several provinces.
• C.R. Das died in 1925; after his death, the Swarajist movement gradually declined.
• The Swarajist experiment ended by 1927, with most members rejoining mainstream Congress.

hi.display_text:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के तहत स्थापित सुधारित काउंसिलों में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस की भागीदारी के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?

(a) स्वराजवादी गुट ने गया सत्र (1922) में काउंसिल प्रवेश के लिए कांग्रेस की मंजूरी प्राप्त की, जिसके बाद C.R. दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू ने बहिष्कार को पलटा।
(b) असहयोग आंदोलन के तहत प्रारंभिक बहिष्कार के बाद, स्वराजवादी गुट ने 1923 में कांग्रेस की नीति पलट दी और स्पष्ट रणनीति के साथ सुधारित काउंसिलों में प्रवेश किया, जिसमें सरकार को भीतर से बाधित करना शामिल था।
(c) स्वराजवादी गुट ने मॉडरेट्स के विपरीत 1920 के दशक में काउंसिलों में प्रवेश करने से इनकार किया, और साइमन कमीशन की घोषणा तक असहयोग बहिष्कार बनाए रखा।
(d) C.R. दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू ने 1923 में 'प्रतिक्रियाशील सहयोग' रणनीति अपनाई, जिसमें काउंसिल की कार्यवाही में बाधा डालने के बजाय रचनात्मक भागीदारी पर सहमति दी।
hi.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प a भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि C.R. दास स्वराजवादी गुट से जुड़े थे, लेकिन 1923 की स्वराजवादी रणनीति को विशेष रूप से 'गया कांग्रेस सत्र' से जोड़ना (जहां C.R. दास ने अपने काउंसिल-प्रवेश प्रस्ताव के हारने पर कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया था) घटना को परिणाम के साथ भ्रमित करता है।
elimination_logic: स्वराजवादी रणनीति की पहचान करें: C.R. दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू ने सुधारित काउंसिलों में प्रवेश कर सरकार को भीतर से बाधित करने का प्रस्ताव रखा — जो असहयोग बहिष्कार से अलग था।
(a) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: स्वराजवादियों को गया कांग्रेस (1922) में मंजूरी नहीं मिली — उनका प्रस्ताव वहां हार गया था, जिसके कारण C.R. दास ने कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया।
(b) विकल्प की पुष्टि करें: स्वराजवादियों ने एक अलग राजनीतिक संगठन बनाया और 1923 में बहिष्कार निर्णय को पलट दिया, उस वर्ष के चुनावों के बाद काउंसिलों में प्रवेश किया।
(c) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: मॉडरेट्स (लिबरल फेडरेशन) — स्वराजवादियों के विपरीत — शुरू से ही भाग लेते थे। स्वराजवादियों ने 1923 में बहिष्कार को पलटा।
(d) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: 'प्रतिक्रियाशील सहयोग' कुछ मध्यम राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा अपनाई गई अलग स्थिति थी; स्वराजवादी रणनीति विशेष रूप से 'भीतर से बाधा' थी — अलग शब्दावली और अलग उद्देश्य।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन ट्रैप में गया कांग्रेस (1922) — जहां स्वराजवादियों ने वोट खोया — को 1923 के पलटाव के साथ मिलाना शामिल है। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि C.R. दास और गया जुड़े हैं, वे बिना यह जाने कि गया हार था, विकल्प (a) को सही चिह्नित कर सकते हैं। स्वराजवादी पलटाव बाद में विशेष कांग्रेस सत्र और अलग राजनीतिक संगठन के माध्यम से आया।
hi.final_explanation:
असहयोग आंदोलन के बहिष्कार ने 1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत स्थापित सुधारित काउंसिलों के प्रति रणनीतिक दुविधा उत्पन्न कर दी थी, खासकर चौरी चौरा घटना (1922) के बाद आंदोलन के निलंबन के बाद। C.R. दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू के नेतृत्व में स्वराजवादी गुट ने बहिष्कार को पलटने और काउंसिलों में प्रवेश कर 'भीतर से सुधारों को विफल करने' की रणनीति अपनाई।

• विकल्प (a): गलत — गया कांग्रेस सत्र (1922) में स्वराजवादी काउंसिल प्रवेश प्रस्ताव हार गया था। C.R. दास ने निराश होकर कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया। पलटाव 1923 में हुआ, गया में नहीं।
• विकल्प (b): सही — 1923 में पर्याप्त समर्थन जीतने के बाद स्वराजवादी सुधारित काउंसिलों में प्रवेश किए। उनकी रणनीति सरकार के कामकाज को विधायिका के भीतर बाधित करना था, सहयोग नहीं।
• विकल्प (c): गलत — शुरू से ही मॉडरेट्स (बाद में लिबरल फेडरेशन) ने भाग लिया, जिन्होंने सुधारों का स्वागत किया। स्वराजवादी केवल 1923 में असहयोग बहिष्कार के बाद शामिल हुए।
• विकल्प (d): गलत — 'प्रतिक्रियाशील सहयोग' अलग मध्यम राष्ट्रवादियों से जुड़ा था; स्वराजवादी रणनीति स्पष्ट रूप से 'भीतर से बाधा' थी, सहयोग नहीं।

Value Addition:
• स्वराजवादियों ने 1923 के चुनावों में महत्वपूर्ण सीटें जीतीं और कई प्रांतों में काउंसिल की कार्यवाही को प्रभावी रूप से ठप कर दिया।
• C.R. दास 1925 में निधन हो गया; उनके बाद स्वराजवादी आंदोलन धीरे-धीरे कमजोर हुआ।
• स्वराजवादी प्रयोग 1927 तक समाप्त हो गया, अधिकांश सदस्य मुख्यधारा कांग्रेस में वापस शामिल हो गए।

shared.concept_anchor: Continuities and breaks between 1919 and 1935 Acts

table_data.header_text: Consider the following statements comparing the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935:
rows: Dyarchy at the provincial level was retained under the Government of India Act 1935.
Both the 1919 Act and the 1935 Act retained communal electorates as a feature of the electoral system.
An All-India Federation including princely states was proposed under the Government of India Act 1919.
The Viceroy's overriding powers were retained under both the 1919 Act and the 1935 Act.
table_data.footer_text:
How many of the above statements are correct?

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three
(d) All four

statement_analysis.statement: Dyarchy at the provincial level was retained under the Government of India Act 1935.
statement_analysis.reason: The 1935 Act abolished dyarchy at the provincial level entirely — provinces received full autonomy. Dyarchy was instead proposed at the Centre under the 1935 Act, though it was never implemented.

statement_analysis.statement: Both the 1919 Act and the 1935 Act retained communal electorates as a feature of the electoral system.
statement_analysis.reason: Communal electorates were a continuity across both Acts — the 1935 Act retained and even elaborated communal representation, including reservations established after the Poona Pact.

statement_analysis.statement: An All-India Federation including princely states was proposed under the Government of India Act 1919.
statement_analysis.reason: The federal structure incorporating princely states was proposed under the Government of India Act 1935, not 1919. The 1919 Act had no federal structure.

statement_analysis.statement: The Viceroy's overriding powers were retained under both the 1919 Act and the 1935 Act.
statement_analysis.reason: Both Acts retained the Viceroy's powers of certification, dissolution, and special responsibilities — the executive superintendence of the Viceroy was a structural continuity across both Acts.

en.strong_distractor: c — Option c (only three correct) is deceptive for students who correctly identify that the 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy but forget that the federal dyarchy proposed in 1935 was never implemented — they may credit Statement 1 as partially correct.
elimination_logic: Statement 1: Dyarchy was abolished at the provincial level by the 1935 Act — not retained. Statement 1 is incorrect.
Statement 2: Communal electorates persisted through both Acts — confirmed continuity. Statement 2 is correct.
Statement 3: An All-India Federation was a 1935 Act proposal, not 1919. Statement 3 is incorrect.
Statement 4: Viceroy's overriding powers were retained in both Acts — confirmed continuity. Statement 4 is correct.
Two correct (Statements 2 and 4) — select option (b): Only two.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 1 is the primary conflation trap — students who know dyarchy was 'shifted' between the two Acts sometimes believe it was retained in some form under 1935. Statement 3 exploits the confusion between the 1935 Act's major innovation (federation) and the 1919 Act's more limited scope. Both errors push students toward overcounting correct statements.
en.final_explanation:
| Statement | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Dyarchy at provincial level retained under 1935 Act | Incorrect — abolished; proposed at Centre but never implemented |
| Both Acts retained communal electorates | Correct — key continuity |
| All-India Federation proposed under 1919 Act | Incorrect — this was a 1935 Act provision |
| Viceroy's overriding powers retained in both Acts | Correct — structural continuity |

Key breaks between 1919 and 1935: Provincial autonomy (1935 abolished provincial dyarchy); federal structure proposed (1935, not 1919); elaborate fiscal federalism (1935). Key continuities: communal electorates, Viceroy's powers, Secretary of State's superintendence.

Value Addition:
• Federal dyarchy under the 1935 Act was never implemented because the princely states did not accede to the federation.
• The 1935 Act's provincial autonomy provisions did come into force — Congress formed governments in 7 provinces after the 1937 elections.
• The 1935 Act remains the longest-ever statute passed by the British Parliament for any territory.

table_data.header_text: 1919 और 1935 के भारत सरकार अधिनियमों की तुलना करते हुए निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
rows: 1935 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतीय स्तर पर द्वि-शासन बरकरार रखा गया।
1919 और 1935 दोनों अधिनियमों ने चुनावी प्रणाली की एक विशेषता के रूप में सामुदायिक मतदाता प्रणाली बरकरार रखी।
1919 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम के तहत रियासतों सहित अखिल-भारतीय संघ प्रस्तावित किया गया था।
1919 और 1935 दोनों अधिनियमों के तहत वायसराय के सर्वोच्च अधिकार बरकरार रखे गए।

उपरोक्त में से कितने कथन सही हैं?

(a) केवल एक
(b) केवल दो
(c) केवल तीन
(d) सभी चार

statement_analysis.statement: Dyarchy at the provincial level was retained under the Government of India Act 1935.
statement_analysis.reason: 1935 का अधिनियम प्रांतीय स्तर पर द्वि-शासन (dyarchy) को पूरी तरह समाप्त कर देता है — प्रांतों को पूर्ण स्वायत्तता मिली। द्वि-शासन केंद्र में 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत प्रस्तावित था, हालांकि इसे कभी लागू नहीं किया गया।

statement_analysis.statement: Both the 1919 Act and the 1935 Act retained communal electorates as a feature of the electoral system.
statement_analysis.reason: सामुदायिक मतदाता प्रणाली दोनों अधिनियमों में निरंतरता थी — 1935 का अधिनियम सामुदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व को बरकरार रखता है और पूना समझौते के बाद स्थापित आरक्षणों सहित इसे विस्तृत करता है।

statement_analysis.statement: An All-India Federation including princely states was proposed under the Government of India Act 1919.
statement_analysis.reason: साम्राज्यवादी राज्यों सहित अखिल-भारतीय संघीय संरचना 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत प्रस्तावित थी, 1919 के अधिनियम में कोई संघीय संरचना नहीं थी।

statement_analysis.reason: दोनों अधिनियमों में वायसराय के प्रमाणन, विघटन और विशेष जिम्मेदारियों के अधिकार बरकरार थे — वायसराय की कार्यकारी पर्यवेक्षण क्षमता दोनों अधिनियमों में संरचनात्मक निरंतरता थी।

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the fiscal provisions introduced under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919:

1. Under the 1919 reforms, customs revenue was assigned exclusively to the Central Government, while land revenue was assigned to provincial governments.
2. Provincial governments under the 1919 reforms could raise loans from any source without requiring the Central Government's approval, as fiscal autonomy was a key concession of the reforms.
3. Income tax was assigned as a shared revenue head between the Centre and provinces under the 1919 provincial settlement.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Under the 1919 reforms, customs revenue was assigned exclusively to the Central Government, while land revenue was assigned to provincial governments.
statement_analysis.reason: Customs (a foreign trade-linked revenue) was a central head, while land revenue — the primary direct tax collected from cultivators — was a provincial head. This division was foundational to the provincial settlement concept.

statement_analysis.statement: Provincial governments under the 1919 reforms could raise loans from any source without requiring the Central Government's approval, as fiscal autonomy was a key concession of the reforms.
statement_analysis.reason: Provincial governments could NOT raise loans without Centre's approval — fiscal autonomy remained curtailed. The ability to borrow independently was not conceded, which is why the 'provincial settlement' was criticized as incomplete.

statement_analysis.statement: Income tax was assigned as a shared revenue head between the Centre and provinces under the 1919 provincial settlement.
statement_analysis.reason: Income tax was a central revenue head under the 1919 provisions, not a shared head. The more elaborate sharing and division came under the 1935 Act and later the Finance Commission framework under the 1950 Constitution.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is deceptive for students who associate the 1919 reforms with genuine fiscal devolution and assume that if land revenue went to provinces, income tax must also have been shared.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Customs → Centre; land revenue → provinces. This is the established division under the 1919 provincial settlement. Statement 1 is correct.
Evaluate Statement 2: Provinces could not borrow independently — central approval was mandatory. 'Fiscal autonomy' was not a genuine concession. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 3: Income tax was a central head, not shared, under the 1919 provisions. Statement 3 is incorrect.
Only Statement 1 is correct — select option (a): 1 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3 uses a geographic-swap trap in the revenue assignment category — swapping income tax from 'Centre only' to 'shared' sounds plausible because income tax sharing became important under later constitutional arrangements. Students familiar with the Finance Commission's income tax sharing provisions may incorrectly backdating this to 1919.
en.final_explanation:
The 1919 reforms attempted a 'provincial settlement' — separating central and provincial finances — but the separation was far from complete.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Customs (including export/import duties) remained a central revenue head; land revenue, excise duties, and other direct provincial taxes were assigned to provinces. This revenue split was the basis of the 1919 fiscal division.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Borrowing autonomy was NOT granted. Provinces required Centre's prior approval for any loans — a significant constraint on their ability to fund transferred subjects independently. This was a continuation of centralized fiscal control.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Income tax was a central (not shared) revenue head under the 1919 provisions. The concept of sharing income tax proceeds with provinces became relevant only under the 1935 Act and was institutionalized by the Finance Commission after 1950.

Value Addition:
• The 1919 'provincial settlement' was the first attempt at systematic fiscal separation — but it was incomplete due to retained central loan approval.
• The 1935 Act created a more elaborate fiscal framework, including provisions for grants-in-aid.
• The Finance Commission under Article 280 of the 1950 Constitution institutionalized the sharing of central taxes (including income tax and Union excise duties) with states.
