en.display_text:
Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional fate of the dyarchy system introduced by the Government of India Act 1919 in relation to the Government of India Act 1935?

(a) Dyarchy was completely abolished at both provincial and central levels under the Government of India Act 1935.
(b) Dyarchy was retained and strengthened at the provincial level under the Government of India Act 1935, while being introduced for the first time at the Centre.
(c) Dyarchy continued at the provincial level and was simultaneously introduced at the central level under both the 1919 and 1935 Acts.
(d) Dyarchy was abolished at the provincial level under the 1935 Act, which instead proposed central dyarchy as part of the federal executive — though this central dyarchy was never implemented.
en.strong_distractor: b — Option b is deceptive because students who know dyarchy was 'abolished at the provincial level' under 1935 may confuse this with a complete elimination of dyarchy from the constitutional framework, without knowing it was proposed (but never implemented) at the Centre.
elimination_logic: Track the fate of dyarchy from 1919 to 1935 and beyond.
Eliminate option (a): Dyarchy was not abolished entirely under the 1935 Act — it was proposed at the Centre in the federal provisions.
Eliminate option (b): Dyarchy was abolished at the provincial level — not retained or strengthened there under 1935.
Eliminate option (c): The 1919 Act had dyarchy only at the provincial level — it was never applied at the Centre under the 1919 Act.

Confirm option (d): The 1935 Act abolished dyarchy at the provincial level (provinces got full autonomy) and proposed dyarchy at the Centre as part of the federal structure — but this federal dyarchy was never implemented because the princely states did not accede.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Students who know 'dyarchy was abolished under the 1935 Act' without knowing its full trajectory will miss the critical distinction: abolished at provincial level, proposed (but never implemented) at the Centre. The entity-swap trap operates by confusing the level (provincial vs central) at which dyarchy was maintained, shifted, or proposed.
en.final_explanation:
Dyarchy's constitutional journey across the 1919 and 1935 Acts is a precise and frequently tested comparison.

• Option (a): Incorrect — dyarchy was not abolished entirely under the 1935 Act. Provincial dyarchy was abolished, but the 1935 Act proposed central dyarchy as part of the federal executive structure.
• Option (b): Incorrect — the 1935 Act specifically abolished dyarchy at the provincial level, replacing it with full provincial autonomy. Provincial ministers no longer had reserved subjects above them.
• Option (c): Incorrect — under the 1919 Act, dyarchy operated only at the provincial level. The Centre had no dyarchy — the Viceroy's Executive Council was entirely unaccountable to the legislature.
• Option (d): Correct — the 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy (provinces gained full autonomy) and proposed central dyarchy as part of the federal executive structure. However, this central dyarchy was never implemented because the required number of princely states did not accede to the All-India Federation.

Value Addition:
• Provincial autonomy under the 1935 Act came into force after the 1937 elections; Congress formed governments in 7 provinces.
• The federal provisions of the 1935 Act (including central dyarchy) never came into force due to the princely states' non-accession.
• The concept of dyarchy — divided executive — has no parallel in the 1950 Constitution, which established full parliamentary government.

en.display_text:
The Montagu Declaration of August 1917, issued by the Secretary of State for India, is significant for explicitly stating the British government's policy goal for India. The Declaration referred to the '________' as the objective of British India policy.

(a) Responsible government for India as a Dominion within the British Empire
(b) Immediate grant of representative institutions leading to full executive accountability
(c) Gradual development of self-governing institutions
(d) Complete transfer of executive authority to elected legislatures within a defined timeframe
en.strong_distractor: a — Option a is deceptive because 'responsible government for India as a Dominion' sounds like a natural culmination of the Declaration's aims, and students who associate the 1917 Declaration with a significant step forward may assume it used more ambitious language.
elimination_logic: The question asks for the exact qualifying language used in the Montagu Declaration of August 1917.
Eliminate option (a): 'Responsible government for India as a Dominion' — the Declaration did not promise Dominion Status. 'Dominion' does not appear in the 1917 Declaration.
Eliminate option (b): 'Immediate grant of representative institutions' — 'immediate' contradicts the Declaration's deliberate use of 'gradual.'
Confirm option (c): 'Gradual development of self-governing institutions' — 'gradual' was the operative qualifier, deliberately chosen to avoid any commitment to rapid transfer of power.
Eliminate option (d): 'Complete transfer of executive authority to elected legislatures' — far too broad and specific; the Declaration made no such commitment.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The scope-extension trap operates through option (a) — 'Dominion' status sounds like a logical escalation from 'responsible government,' and students who know the Declaration used ambitious language may assume it went as far as Dominion Status. Critically, Dominion Status was the demand of the nationalist movement — not what the 1917 Declaration offered. The Declaration's language was carefully hedged with 'gradual,' which is the precise term UPSC tests.
en.final_explanation:
The Montagu Declaration of August 1917 is significant as the first explicit British acknowledgment that responsible self-government for India was a policy objective — but its qualifying language was deliberately cautious.

• Option (a): 'Responsible government for India as a Dominion' — Incorrect. The Declaration did not use the word 'Dominion.' Dominion Status was the demand nationalists pressed for; the British explicitly declined to offer it in 1917.
• Option (b): 'Immediate grant of representative institutions' — Incorrect. 'Immediate' contradicts the exact language of the Declaration. The word 'gradual' was placed precisely to signal that any constitutional progress would be incremental and on British terms.
• Option (c): 'Gradual development of self-governing institutions' — Correct. This was the core phrase, accompanied by 'increasing association of Indians in every branch of the administration.' The word 'gradual' was the most debated element of the Declaration.
• Option (d): 'Complete transfer of executive authority to elected legislatures' — Incorrect. This level of commitment was never made in 1917; full executive accountability came only with the 1950 Constitution.

Value Addition:
• Full text of the key phrase: 'increasing association of Indians in every branch of the administration and the gradual development of self-governing institutions.'
• The Montagu Declaration is also called the 'August Declaration' of 1917.
• The gap between 'gradual development' (1917) and actual responsible government (1950) spans 33 years — a measure of how hedged the Declaration truly was.

hi.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प a भ्रामक है क्योंकि 'भारत के लिए डोमिनियन के रूप में जिम्मेदार सरकार' घोषणा के उद्देश्यों की स्वाभाविक परिणति जैसा लगता है, और जो छात्र 1917 की घोषणा को एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम मानते हैं वे मान सकते हैं कि इसमें अधिक महत्वाकांक्षी भाषा का उपयोग हुआ।
elimination_logic: प्रश्न में अगस्त 1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा में प्रयुक्त सटीक योगात्मक भाषा मांगी गई है।
(a) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: 'भारत के लिए डोमिनियन के रूप में जिम्मेदार सरकार' — घोषणा में डोमिनियन स्थिति का वादा नहीं किया गया था। 'डोमिनियन' शब्द 1917 की घोषणा में नहीं है।
(b) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: 'प्रतिनिधि संस्थाओं का तत्काल अनुदान' — 'तत्काल' शब्द घोषणा में प्रयुक्त 'क्रमिक' शब्द के विपरीत है।
(c) विकल्प की पुष्टि करें: 'स्वशासित संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास' — 'क्रमिक' वह मुख्य योगात्मक शब्द था, जो सत्ता के शीघ्र हस्तांतरण के लिए कोई प्रतिबद्धता न देने के लिए जानबूझकर चुना गया था।
(d) विकल्प को निरस्त करें: 'निर्धारित समय सीमा में निर्वाचित विधानसभाओं को कार्यकारी अधिकारों का पूर्ण हस्तांतरण' — यह बहुत व्यापक और विशिष्ट है; घोषणा में ऐसी कोई प्रतिबद्धता नहीं थी।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन ट्रैप विकल्प (a) के माध्यम से काम करता है — 'डोमिनियन' स्थिति 'जिम्मेदार सरकार' से तार्किक उन्नति लगती है, और जो छात्र जानते हैं कि घोषणा में महत्वाकांक्षी भाषा थी वे मान सकते हैं कि यह डोमिनियन स्थिति तक गई। महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि डोमिनियन स्थिति राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन की मांग थी — 1917 की घोषणा ने इसे नहीं दिया। घोषणा की भाषा सावधानीपूर्वक 'क्रमिक' शब्द से सीमित की गई थी, जो UPSC द्वारा परखा जाता है।
hi.final_explanation:
अगस्त 1917 की मोंटागु घोषणा महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह पहली बार स्पष्ट रूप से ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा भारत के लिए जिम्मेदार स्वशासन को नीति लक्ष्य के रूप में स्वीकार किया गया — लेकिन इसकी योगात्मक भाषा जानबूझकर सतर्क थी।

• विकल्प (a): 'भारत के लिए डोमिनियन के रूप में जिम्मेदार सरकार' — गलत। घोषणा में 'डोमिनियन' शब्द का उपयोग नहीं हुआ। डोमिनियन स्थिति राष्ट्रीयतावादियों की मांग थी; ब्रिटिशों ने 1917 में इसे स्पष्ट रूप से अस्वीकार किया।
• विकल्प (b): 'प्रतिनिधि संस्थाओं का तत्काल अनुदान' — गलत। 'तत्काल' शब्द घोषणा की सटीक भाषा के विपरीत है। 'क्रमिक' शब्द इस बात का संकेत था कि संवैधानिक प्रगति धीरे-धीरे और ब्रिटिश शर्तों पर होगी।
• विकल्प (c): 'स्वशासित संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास' — सही। यह मुख्य वाक्यांश था, जिसके साथ 'प्रशासन के प्रत्येक शाखा में भारतीयों की बढ़ती भागीदारी' भी थी। 'क्रमिक' शब्द घोषणा का सबसे विवादित तत्व था।
• विकल्प (d): 'निर्धारित समय सीमा में निर्वाचित विधानसभाओं को कार्यकारी अधिकारों का पूर्ण हस्तांतरण' — गलत। 1917 में ऐसी प्रतिबद्धता नहीं थी; पूर्ण कार्यकारी जवाबदेही केवल 1950 के संविधान के साथ आई।

Value Addition:
• मुख्य वाक्यांश का पूर्ण पाठ: 'प्रशासन के प्रत्येक शाखा में भारतीयों की बढ़ती भागीदारी और स्वशासित संस्थाओं का क्रमिक विकास।'
• मोंटागु घोषणा को 1917 की 'अगस्त घोषणा' भी कहा जाता है।
• 'क्रमिक विकास' (1917) और वास्तविक जिम्मेदार सरकार (1950) के बीच 33 वर्षों का अंतर है — जो घोषणा की सतर्कता को दर्शाता है।

shared.concept_anchor: Key features of 1919 Act matched to their correct descriptions

table_data.header_text: Match List I (Feature of the Government of India Act 1919) with List II (Correct Description):
rows: A. Dyarchy
1. A new office in London handling commercial matters, appointed by Government of India
B. High Commissioner for India
2. Left to provincial discretion; Madras was the first province to grant it in 1921
C. Central Public Service Commission provision
3. Division of provincial subjects into reserved (Governor) and transferred (ministers)
D. Women's franchise
4. Statutory basis in 1919 Act; actual establishment in 1926 following Lee Commission recommendation
table_data.footer_text:
Which of the following is the correct matching?

(a) A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4
(b) A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4
(c) A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2
(d) A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2

en.strong_distractor: b — Option b is deceptive because it correctly pairs dyarchy and the High Commissioner but swaps the PSC provision with the franchise description, exploiting the fact that both are 1919 Act features that students may not associate precisely.
elimination_logic: Match A (Dyarchy): Division of provincial subjects into reserved (Governor + Executive Council) and transferred (ministers responsible to legislature) — match A-3.
Match B (High Commissioner for India): A new London-based office for commercial functions, appointed by Government of India — match B-1.
Match C (Central Public Service Commission): Statutory basis provided in 1919, actual establishment in 1926 after Lee Commission recommendation — match C-4.
Match D (Women's franchise): Left to provincial discretion, with Madras being the first province to exercise it in 1921 — match D-2.
Correct combination: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2 — select option (d).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap works by associating the High Commissioner with political functions (swapped from Secretary of State) or the PSC with immediate establishment (confusing provision with implementation). Option (b) tests whether students know the High Commissioner's appointment authority (Government of India, not Crown) and whether they separate the PSC statutory provision (1919) from its actual establishment (1926).
en.final_explanation:
This question tests precise knowledge of four distinct features of the Government of India Act 1919.

Correct matches:
• A (Dyarchy) → 3 (Division into reserved and transferred subjects): Dyarchy's defining mechanism was this bifurcation of provincial administration — reserved subjects under Governor, transferred subjects under elected ministers.
• B (High Commissioner for India) → 1 (London-based office for commercial functions, appointed by Government of India): The High Commissioner handled trade/commercial matters; political authority remained with the Secretary of State. Crucially, the appointing authority was the Government of India, not the Crown.
• C (Central Public Service Commission) → 4 (Statutory basis in 1919, established 1926 after Lee Commission): The seven-year gap between provision and implementation, bridged by the Lee Commission, is the key fact.
• D (Women's franchise) → 2 (Left to provincial discretion; Madras first in 1921): No uniform provision; provincial legislatures decided independently. Madras exercised this discretion first.

Trap pairings: Options swapping B and C exploit confusion between the High Commissioner's commercial role and the PSC's administrative role. Options swapping C and D exploit confusion between franchise provisions and administrative commission provisions.

Value Addition:
• All four features — dyarchy, High Commissioner, PSC provision, women's franchise by discretion — were criticized as half-measures.
• Universal women's franchise arrived only in 1950 with the Constitution of India.
• The High Commissioner for India (London) predates the modern diplomatic High Commissioner concept that emerged post-Independence.

hi.strong_distractor: b — Option b is deceptive because it correctly pairs dyarchy and the High Commissioner but swaps the PSC provision with the franchise description, exploiting the fact that both are 1919 Act features that students may not associate precisely.
elimination_logic: A (ड्योरकी) से मेल करें: प्रांतीय विषयों का विभाजन आरक्षित (गवर्नर + कार्यकारी परिषद) और हस्तांतरित (मंत्रियों की जिम्मेदारी विधायिका के प्रति) — A-3 से मेल करें।
B (भारत के उच्चायुक्त) से मेल करें: वाणिज्यिक कार्यों के लिए लंदन में नया कार्यालय, भारत सरकार द्वारा नियुक्त — B-1 से मेल करें।
C (केंद्रीय लोक सेवा आयोग प्रावधान) से मेल करें: 1919 में वैधानिक आधार प्रदान किया गया, ली आयोग की सिफारिश के बाद 1926 में वास्तविक स्थापना — C-4 से मेल करें।
D (महिला मताधिकार) से मेल करें: प्रांतीय विवेकाधिकार पर छोड़ा गया, मद्रास ने 1921 में इसे पहली बार लागू किया — D-2 से मेल करें।

hi.upsc_trap_explanation: इकाई-स्थानांतरण जाल उच्चायुक्त को राजनीतिक कार्यों से जोड़कर (जो सचिव राज्य से स्थानांतरित है) या लोक सेवा आयोग को तत्काल स्थापना से जोड़कर (प्रावधान को क्रियान्वयन से भ्रमित करके) काम करता है। विकल्प (b) यह परखता है कि छात्र जानते हैं कि उच्चायुक्त की नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी भारत सरकार है, क्राउन नहीं, और वे लोक सेवा आयोग के वैधानिक प्रावधान (1919) को उसकी वास्तविक स्थापना (1926) से अलग करते हैं।
hi.final_explanation:
यह प्रश्न भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 की चार विशिष्ट विशेषताओं का सटीक ज्ञान परखता है।

सही मेल:
• A (ड्योरकी) → 3 (आरक्षित और हस्तांतरित विषयों में विभाजन): ड्योरकी की परिभाषित प्रक्रिया प्रांतीय प्रशासन का यह द्विभाजन था — आरक्षित विषय गवर्नर के अधीन, हस्तांतरित विषय निर्वाचित मंत्रियों के अधीन।
• B (भारत के उच्चायुक्त) → 1 (लंदन स्थित कार्यालय, वाणिज्यिक कार्यों के लिए, भारत सरकार द्वारा नियुक्त): उच्चायुक्त ने व्यापार/वाणिज्यिक मामलों को संभाला; राजनीतिक अधिकार सचिव राज्य के पास रहे। महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी भारत सरकार था, क्राउन नहीं।
• C (केंद्रीय लोक सेवा आयोग) → 4 (1919 अधिनियम में वैधानिक आधार; ली आयोग की सिफारिश के बाद 1926 में स्थापना): प्रावधान और क्रियान्वयन के बीच सात वर्ष का अंतर, जो ली आयोग द्वारा पाटी गई, मुख्य तथ्य है।
• D (महिला मताधिकार) → 2 (प्रांतीय विवेकाधिकार पर छोड़ा गया; मद्रास ने 1921 में पहली बार इसे लागू किया): कोई एकरूप प्रावधान नहीं था; प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं ने स्वतंत्र रूप से निर्णय लिया। मद्रास ने यह विवेकाधिकार सबसे पहले प्रयोग किया।

जाल जोड़ी: विकल्प जो B और C को स्थानांतरित करते हैं, वे उच्चायुक्त के वाणिज्यिक भूमिका और लोक सेवा आयोग के प्रशासनिक भूमिका के बीच भ्रम का लाभ उठाते हैं। विकल्प जो C और D को स्थानांतरित करते हैं, वे मताधिकार प्रावधानों और प्रशासनिक आयोग प्रावधानों के बीच भ्रम का लाभ उठाते हैं।

Value Addition:
• ये चारों विशेषताएँ — ड्योरकी, उच्चायुक्त, लोक सेवा आयोग प्रावधान, प्रांतीय विवेकाधिकार द्वारा महिला मताधिकार — आधे-अधूरे उपाय के रूप में आलोचना की गईं।
• सार्वभौमिक महिला मताधिकार केवल 1950 में भारत के संविधान के साथ आया।
• भारत के उच्चायुक्त (लंदन) आधुनिक राजनयिक उच्चायुक्त की अवधारणा से पहले अस्तित्व में था, जो स्वतंत्रता के बाद उभरी।

shared.concept_anchor: Structural innovations of the 1919 Act: declaration, bicameralism, elected majority

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the structural features of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms:

1. The Montagu-Chelmsford Report of 1918, which formed the basis for the Government of India Act 1919, was co-authored by Edwin Montagu as Secretary of State for India and Lord Chelmsford as Viceroy of India.
2. The Council of State, introduced as the Upper House of the central legislature under the 1919 Act, had a total of 145 members of whom 105 were elected.
3. Under the Government of India Act 1919, elected members formed a majority in provincial legislative councils for the first time in colonial India's constitutional history.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report of 1918, which formed the basis for the Government of India Act 1919, was co-authored by Edwin Montagu as Secretary of State for India and Lord Chelmsford as Viceroy of India.
statement_analysis.reason: Edwin Montagu held the office of Secretary of State and Lord Chelmsford was the concurrent Viceroy — both co-authored the Report published in 1918. This is the most commonly confused role-attribution in this topic.

statement_analysis.statement: The Council of State, introduced as the Upper House of the central legislature under the 1919 Act, had a total of 145 members of whom 105 were elected.
statement_analysis.reason: These figures (145 total, 105 elected) belong to the Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House), not the Council of State. The Council of State had 60 members, of whom 27 were elected — the numbers are the classic swap trap.

statement_analysis.statement: Under the Government of India Act 1919, elected members formed a majority in provincial legislative councils for the first time in colonial India's constitutional history.
statement_analysis.reason: The 1919 Act made elected members a majority in provincial councils — a departure from the Morley-Minto framework that retained an official nominated majority.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is deceptive because Statements 1 and 3 are fully accurate; students who are uncertain about the numbers in Statement 2 and recall 'those are 1919 Act numbers' may assume Statement 2 is also correct.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Montagu as Secretary of State + Chelmsford as Viceroy + 1918 Report — all correct. Statement 1 is correct.

Evaluate Statement 2: 145 total and 105 elected are the figures for the Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House), not the Council of State (Upper House). The Council of State had 60 members, 27 elected. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 3: Elected majority in provincial councils first achieved under 1919 Act — correct. Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 1 and 3 correct — select option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses a partial-truth trap: the numbers 145 and 105 are real, genuine figures from the 1919 Act — but they belong to the wrong chamber. Assigning the Lower House's composition to the Upper House is the trap. Students who recall 'the 1919 Act had 145 members with 105 elected' but do not specify which house will mark Statement 2 as correct.
en.final_explanation:
Three dimensions of the 1919 Act are tested simultaneously in this question.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Edwin Montagu was Secretary of State for India; Lord Chelmsford was Viceroy of India. These two officials co-authored the Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) that became the basis for the Government of India Act 1919. Swapping their offices is the most common role-attribution error for this topic.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: 145 total members (105 elected) describes the Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House). The Council of State (Upper House) had 60 total members, of whom 27 were elected. Assigning the Lower House numbers to the Upper House is the numerical trap.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The Morley-Minto Act (1909) retained an official nominated majority in provincial councils. The 1919 Act made elected members a majority — a significant structural shift, though qualified by the Governor's retained override powers.

Value Addition:
• The Council of State (Upper House) had higher property qualifications for voters and candidates — making it more conservative in composition.
• The Morley-Minto framework's official majority meant that even when Indians formed a plurality, they were outvoted by appointed officials.
• The 1919 Act's elected majority in provincial councils was a prerequisite for the ministerial accountability that dyarchy required.
